text:
andrew: quick heads-up — ran a targeted perf sweep on the kv cache yesterday against long-context chat (seq_len=4096, batch=8). Observed steady memory climb ~160MB over 90s and prefix hit rate collapsing to ~18% under synthetic churn. p95 token latency +12ms relative to baseline. attaching short logs and a flame snapshot (link).

mira: can you paste the minimal repro/log snippet here? curious if this is eviction churn or just key proliferation.

andrew: log excerpt:
```
kv_store:alloc_pages +63MB @ 0.12s
kv_store:evict_batch start sz=48 keys
kv_store:evict_batch end freed=4
kv:lookup miss prefix=k:tenant:session:conv123:prefixhash
kv:insert size=512KB
mem.total 1280MB -> 1440MB
```

kevin: that pattern (many small frees, few reclaimed) smells like fragmentation + small-object churn. Did we change key shape recently?

andrew: yes — PR 412 changed the prefix key canonicalization: we added a per-request salt to avoid rare cross-tenant collisions when using shared pooled namespaces. Before it was per-session salt.

mira: ah ok. per-request salt would blow up distinct key count a lot. That explains insert rate. Could also force eviction to scan more.

kevin: confirmed locally: toggling salt->session reduces unique keys by ~6x on our replay. Memory growth drops to ~20MB over same window and prefix hit jumps to ~62%. p95 improves ~6ms.

andrew: interesting tradeoff. collision risk vs cache reuse. For product tenants with many short-lived requests, per-request salt was safer but kills reuse.

mira: alternative: keep per-request salt but restrict it to tenant namespace only, not include session/prefix fingerprint. e.g. key = "tenant:<salt>|prefix:<fingerprint>" so identical prefixes across a session still coalesce. Could also add a cheap fingerprint normalization: trim trailing context ids for longctx mode.

kevin: also want to call out eviction unit: our current page allocator has 64KB slabs. Small 512B entries cause fragmentation; we end up with lots of tiny allocations. We should try compacting free lists or using size-classed arenas for small entries.

andrew: did a quick experiment changing stickiness policy: session-sticky + tenant-salted keys + small arena reduces fragmentation and keeps safety. Repro numbers: unique_keys/time -70%, mem-growth +18MB, prefix_hit ~58%, p95 -5ms.

ci-bot: perf-checker: run perf/regression/kv_salting_stickiness on nikola/longctx-replay. Status: queued.

mira: nice. Two follow-ups: 1) add metric kv.prefix_reuse_by_scope with labels {scope=session|request|tenant} to quantify in prod, 2) craft a canary config to test session-sticky default on 10% of traffic for 48h.

kevin: I'll prototype arena allocator patch and a compaction path that triggers when free_fragmentation_ratio > 0.6. Quick microbench shows compaction cost ~3-6ms once per 10k evictions.

andrew: I'll open a non-breaking flagged revert for PR 412 to restore session-salt semantics behind feature flag and run canary. Also will add histograms for kv.eviction_scan_time and kv.fragmentation_ratio.

mira: action items summarized:
- andrew: feature-flag revert + metrics (kv.prefix_reuse_by_scope, kv.eviction_scan_time, kv.fragmentation_ratio) — canary 10% for 48h (due: EOD Fri)
- kevin: arena allocator PR + compaction trigger + microbench notes (due: next Tue)
- mira: create dashboard + alert for prefix_reuse_by_scope < 40% and fragmentation_ratio > 0.5 (due: Mon)

andrew: pinging infra to schedule a canary window. ops-bot canary request in #eng-infra this morning.

ops-bot: deploy-request: canary group "kv-stickiness-expt" created at 1723456900 for service runtime-kv, size=2, duration=48h, traffic=10% :rocket:

kevin: thanks — one more note: please don't rotate salt semantics until we confirm cross-tenant collision rate is actually non-zero in prod. We patched for an extremely rare edgecase; reuse seems more beneficial overall.

mira: agreed. we'll proceed conservatively. thanks for the repro and numbers, andrew — this was helpful.

andrew: cool, I'll post the canary link and perf dashboard once live. :thumbsup:
